title: Pontotoc Electric asks members to test carbon monoxide alarms and check expiration dates
excerpt: Pontotoc Electric issued its reminder Friday. A generator used during an outage should run outdoors, at least 20 feet from doors, windows and garages.
locality: Pontotoc Electric Power Association service area in Mississippi.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc Electric Power Association is asking members to check two things on their carbon monoxide alarms as colder weather brings people indoors. Test the alarm each month and check the device’s expiration date, the cooperative said in a Friday, Nov. 20, safety notice.

Where an alarm sits matters. The U.S. Fire Administration recommends one on every floor of the home and outside each separate sleeping area. A furnace or heater that fails to vent properly can expose people to carbon monoxide, a poisonous gas they cannot see or smell.

For members who use a portable generator during an outage, the cooperative says to take it outdoors and keep it out of enclosed spaces. The National Weather Service gives a distance to allow when choosing a spot outside. Keep the generator at least 20 feet from any door, window or garage. The Fire Administration also advises keeping it away from vents.

Households can also check the places where exhaust leaves the building. The Fire Administration lists vents for the furnace, fireplace, stove and clothes dryer among the openings to keep clear of snow and other debris.
